label: Start infra
description: Bring up a copy of an infra node: the program's own, or with `instance` that instance's copy of a `@per_instance` node. `done` fires once it answers, so the triggers reading it can be activated next. The run waits without holding a worker; a copy that fails to come up fails the node with the reason; an already-running copy is left as is. If you want to answer a caller fast (a route replying 202), turn `waitUntilRunning` off and reply after this node: it finishes as soon as weft accepts the start, and a status read right after shows the copy as `provisioning`.

inputs.name: node
inputs.description: The infra node, named as the program writes it (`bridge`, `work.bridge` inside a group, or `one.bridge` inside an included file): a shared one when `instance` is unwired, one marked `@per_instance` when it is set.

inputs.name: instance
inputs.description: Whose copy: an instance id your program gives it (`user-42`), for that instance's copy of a `@per_instance` node. Unwired: the program's own copy. Wired, and no id arrives (the step feeding it did not run): this node skips.

inputs.name: waitUntilRunning
inputs.label: Wait until running
inputs.description: On: `done` fires once the copy runs, and a copy that fails to come up fails the node. Off: `done` fires once weft accepts the start (a start refused for a passing reason, such as a build in progress, is asked again until it is), and whether the copy then comes up is for a status read to tell.

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: True once the copy is running, or once weft accepted the start when `waitUntilRunning` is off.

then.message: StartInfra '{id}' names {names} in `node`, which is no infra node of this program marked `@per_instance`. It is given an `instance`, so it acts on that instance's copy: name one the way the program writes it (`bridge`, `work.bridge` inside a group, or `one.bridge` inside an included file), or leave `instance` unwired to act on the program's own copy of a shared one.

StartInfra '{id}' names {names} in `node`, which is no shared infra node of this program. It has no `instance`, so it acts on the program's own copy: name one the way the program writes it (`bridge`, `work.bridge` inside a group, or `one.bridge` inside an included file), or wire `instance` to act on an instance's copy of a `@per_instance` one.
